public_record: On 18 December 2017, at meeting S/PV.8139, the Security Council considered Egypt's draft S/2017/1060 on Jerusalem, submitted on behalf of the Group of Arab States. The draft received 14 votes in favour, one against and no abstentions. The sole negative vote came from the United States. The chair declared the draft unadopted because of the negative vote of a permanent member. The failed draft created no new Council obligations.
public_criteria: Identify the draft and Egypt as submitter for the Group of Arab States.
Report the 14–1–0 tally and identify the sole negative vote.
Record that the unsuccessful vote did not create new obligations.

focuses.probe: Check the draft's operative text on Jerusalem and diplomatic missions, as opposed to a delegation's speech.
focuses.mission: Reconstruct the proposed provision in Egypt's unadopted draft concerning changes to Jerusalem's status and the establishment of embassies.
focuses.slip: The proposed language on Jerusalem and diplomatic missions was in Egypt's unadopted draft S/2017/1060.
focuses.backup: Operative paragraph 1 would have declared ineffective and called for rescission of decisions purporting to alter Jerusalem's character, status or demographic composition. It also would have called on States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem, citing resolution 478 (1980).
criteria: Identify the provision as part of the unadopted Egyptian draft.
Identify operative paragraph 1.
Preserve all three categories of proposed changes and their lack of effect.
Preserve the call for rescission.
Name the diplomatic-mission provision and its reference to resolution 478 (1980).

focuses.probe: Check Nikki Haley's national statement after the vote, including the United States' explanation of its veto.
focuses.mission: Reconstruct the U.S. representative's account of the embassy decision and negotiations in explaining her country's negative vote.
focuses.slip: Nikki Haley gave the United States' explanation of its negative vote following the ballot.
focuses.backup: Haley said the veto defended U.S. sovereignty and its role in the Middle East peace process. She asserted that the United States decides where to locate its embassy. She said recognizing Jerusalem did not prejudge the city's final status or the boundaries to be negotiated by the parties.
criteria: Identify Haley's national explanation of the negative vote.
Attribute the sovereignty rationale to Haley.
Preserve the stated U.S. role in the peace process.
Preserve her embassy-siting assertion as a delegation position.
Distinguish recognition from final status and boundaries, with negotiation reserved to the parties.

focuses.probe: Check the United Kingdom's explanation of its affirmative vote, as delivered by Matthew Rycroft.
focuses.mission: Reconstruct how Britain justified supporting the draft in its national explanation, including its position on the city and its own embassy.
focuses.slip: Matthew Rycroft gave the United Kingdom's explanation for its affirmative vote.
focuses.backup: Rycroft said the draft was consistent with previous Council resolutions and the United Kingdom's established position. He said Jerusalem's status should be negotiated and that the city should ultimately serve as the capital of both States. He disagreed with the U.S. recognition and embassy move and said the British Embassy remained in Tel Aviv, with no plans to relocate it.
criteria: Identify Rycroft's national explanation of the affirmative vote.
Preserve both the previous Council resolutions and the established national position.
Preserve negotiated status and the shared-capital position.
Attribute the disagreement with recognition and embassy relocation to Britain.
Identify the embassy location and absence of a plan to relocate.

focuses.probe: Check Olof Skoog's national explanation of Sweden's vote in favour.
focuses.mission: Reconstruct Sweden's public reasons for supporting the draft and its account of the effect of the vote on earlier Council decisions.
focuses.slip: Olof Skoog provided Sweden's explanation of its vote in favour of the draft.
focuses.backup: Skoog said Jerusalem's final status should be negotiated in line with relevant UN resolutions. He supported the proposed restriction on diplomatic missions under resolution 478 (1980) and said the failure of the draft did not affect already adopted Council resolutions.
criteria: Identify Skoog's national explanation of the affirmative vote.
Preserve Sweden's description of Jerusalem as a final-status issue.
Preserve negotiation in line with relevant UN resolutions.
Preserve support for the diplomatic-missions provision and the reference to resolution 478 (1980).
Preserve Sweden's distinction between the failed draft and earlier adopted resolutions.

guard: Fail for an invented vote or rationale, treating draft text as Council action, misidentifying the actor or document, or suggesting the vote itself changed existing Council authority.
question: Can you send the certified working file for this review?
